task: T2 — TBC ownership audit / root cause

crash_root_cause.symptom: SIGSEGV in closeBytecodeUpvaluesFrom (vm.zig:8014) during coroutine.close of a thread suspended inside lua_pcallk with a marked lua_toclose slot (repro: /tmp/opencode/t6_repro.c variant A; PUC: close_calls=1)
crash_root_cause.failing_transition: builtinCoroutineClose -> forced close transport -> appendBytecodeUnwind(disposition=propagate-to-boundary) -> continueBytecodeErrorUnwind frame-popping loop (vm.zig:~12145)
crash_root_cause.invariant_violated: The unwind loop reads frame.u.lua.hasOpenUpvalues() and closeBytecodeUpvaluesFrom(frame, 0) UNCONDITIONALLY on every popped frame. The suspended thread's call_frames contain a C frame (the pcallk CallInfo pushed by callCFunction). Reading u.lua through a frame whose active union arm is u.c yields garbage frame_cap -> bc_boxed[base .. base+garbage_cap] OOB slice -> SIGSEGV at the boxed[i] deref.
crash_root_cause.classification: stale-owner: the unwind machinery assumes all frames are Lua frames; C frames on the same FrameStack are invisible to it

D1_freed_not_closed.behavior: clsret_state.remaining_tbc Values are FREED (alloc.destroy) without running __close during forced-close/reset of a suspended C activation
D1_freed_not_closed.puc: luaE_resetthread: resetCI drops CallInfos; luaD_closeprotected -> luaF_close walks the THREAD-OWNED tbclist independently -> __close runs with (obj, nil)

D2_normal_resume_drop.behavior: the yield-snapshot (remaining_tbc) is freed on successful resume WITHOUT closing; snapshotYieldedTbc already popped the c_toclose_slots marks -> the close obligation vanishes
D2_normal_resume_drop.puc: moveresults sees CIST_TBC -> luaF_close(CLOSEKTOP) at poscall -> __close runs exactly once

old_ownership.owner_of_value: whichever temp c_stack is active in Vm.cur_c_stack (swapped per callCFunction; freed on yield by errdefer)
old_ownership.owner_after_yield: CClsretState.remaining_tbc (heap copy per C frame) — DUPLICATE representation
problems: VM-global indices are meaningful only relative to the currently-swapped temp stack (another thread / nested C call / post-yield = stale indices)
two semantic representations of the same obligation (live marks + yield snapshot)
C-frame discard destroys the obligation (D1) or normal resume drops it (D2)
unwind loop cannot see C frames (D3)

new_ownership.decision: Option B+: per-THREAD TBC chain with slot-identity preserved through frame-owned parked stacks
new_ownership.owner_of_chain: Thread.c_tbc_chain: ArrayListUnmanaged(TbcEntry) where TbcEntry = { cframe_idx: usize, slot_idx: usize }
new_ownership.owner_of_value: the owning C frame's c_stack slice — LIVE while the C fn runs (mutable through the C API = PUC slot semantics), PARKED on the C frame (u.c.parked_stack) across yield/pcallk-error instead of freed
new_ownership.flags: CIST_TBC (bit 18, currently MISSING in vm.zig — PUC lstate.h) set on the C frame at first lua_toclose; CIST_CLSRET means close-was-interrupted-by-yield (already exists)
close_sites: normal C return / finishCcall success: close entries with cframe == this frame, top-down, live stack
finishpcallk error path: same entries with the error object
discardCFrame / reset / lua_closethread: walk the WHOLE thread chain LIFO; resolve values from parked stacks; close; then free
lua_closeslot: only the TOP entry, entry must belong to the current frame
new_ownership.unwind_loop_fix: isC() guard: C frames are popped via the thread-chain close (no u.lua reads)

rejected_alternative: Option A (persistent per-state C stack segments): closest to PUC but requires reworking every C-API indexing assumption across the c_api surface — too broad for this phase's correctness budget; Option B+ preserves the same OWNERSHIP semantics (one chain, slot identity, no snapshots) with a bounded refactor
